definitions.explanation: A corner or out-of-the-way spot. An informal, slightly childish variant of 隅 that adds a sense of smallness or coziness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{部屋|へや}→部屋：00507_heya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{隅|すみ}っこ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}った→座る：00757_suwaru⟧。
examples.english: I sat in the corner of the room.

examples.japanese: ⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{隅|すみ}っこ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{丸|まる}く→丸い：02967_marui⟧⟦なっている→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The cat is curled up in the corner.

examples.japanese: ⟦{教室|きょうしつ}→教室：00794_kyoushitsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{隅|すみ}っこ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{座|すわ}っている→座る：00757_suwaru⟧⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧がいた。
examples.english: There was a kid who always sat alone in the corner of the classroom.

notes:
{隅|すみ}っこ is a casual, diminutive form of ⟦{隅|すみ}→隅：01625_sumi⟧ (corner). The っこ suffix adds a sense of smallness and is common in informal speech.

The word has gained wider recognition through the popular San-X character franchise 「すみっコぐらし」(Sumikko Gurashi), which features characters who like to gather in corners.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{隅|すみ}→隅：01625_sumi⟧: corner — the standard, neutral form
- ⟦{角|かど}→角：02195_kado⟧: corner — refers to an outer corner or angle, while ⟦{隅|すみ}→隅：01625_sumi⟧ is an inner corner
- ⟦{片隅|かたすみ}→片隅：13464_katasumi⟧: a secluded corner — more literary
